script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this is form-only. Over two games BUF has the explosive offense (Cook 34 carries/192 yards, 5.65 YPC; Allen 16/96; Kincaid 14 targets/225 yards) while Herbert is -0.86 EPA/dropback on 14 blitzed dropbacks versus +0.09 unblitzed and BUF blitzes 33%. Base lean: LAC's run defense (3.14 YPC, only 3 runs of 10+) stuffs Cook's efficiency, BUF moves the ball with Allen's pass game instead, and LAC drives shorten when the blitz arrives, so Cook posts a mid-teens carry day nearer 55-70 rush yards than a shootout or a clock-grind.
script.flip1: BUF hits early explosives — LAC has allowed 10.22 YPA on 27 left-side attempts — and leads by multiple scores, so Cook's carries climb into the low 20s and the rush under dies on volume even at a modest YPC.
script.flip2: LAC handles the 33% blitz, Hampton (35 carries, 137 yards) controls the clock, and BUF falls behind and throws. Cook's carries shrink and the under cashes, while BUF pass-catchers become the path to points.

matchup.overlap: Cook does not attack a weak spot: his 5.65 YPC runs into the best run defense in the pack (3.14 YPC, 3 explosive runs). Johnston leads LAC in targets (11) and air yards (103) but has 24 receiving yards; BUF's bleed is the middle (9.41 YPA), not a deep outside shot, and the 33% blitz is a bad overlap for that air-yard role. Kincaid is BUF's primary target (14/225/182 air) but LAC's bleed is the left, not the middle (5.64), and no alignment charting confirms he attacks the left — overlap unconfirmed, so he is not a leg.

form: Window is weeks 1-2 only (labeled L3, two games played); no similar-defense splits and no OC/QB change in the pack. Cook 17 carries/game at 5.65 YPC plus 7 targets/16 yards/-3 air — dump-offs, not a receiving weapon; the 192 rush yards may be opponent-inflated and there are no game splits to see one long run. Allen already has 16 carries/96 yards, a real vulture share. Johnston 11 targets/24 yards/103 air is a miss profile, not a quiet role. McConkey is the LAC producer (10/117/131). Kincaid 14/225/182 and Coleman 8/64/52 versus lines of 57.5 and 14.5 look like chunk-play or missing-context gaps; neither is a leg because that would be average-picking, and Coleman has no injury note to explain a 14.5 line. Hampton 35/137 is the LAC carry share at 3.91 YPC.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Cook's 192 yards on 34 carries is a 5.65 YPC number, and LAC has allowed 3.14 YPC with only 3 runs of 10+, so a stable 16-18 carry day lands nearer 55-70 than the 80.5 line.
edge_players.must_be_true: LAC's run defense stays near that 3.14 YPC / low-explosive profile, Cook's share stays in the mid-teens rather than a blowout 22+, and Allen (16 carries, 96 yards) keeps taking designed runs.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip 1: BUF leads big early and Cook grinds 20-plus carries, or he keeps anything like 5.65 YPC and clears 80.5 on two explosives. At 22 carries even 4.0 YPC is 88.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Johnston has 11 targets and 103 air yards but only 24 receiving yards, and BUF's 33% blitz meets a QB at -0.86 EPA per blitzed dropback, which kills deep WR yards instead of unlocking them.
edge_players.must_be_true: BUF blitzes near 33%, Herbert does not suddenly solve pressure, and Johnston does not turn the air yards into one 40-yard catch.
edge_players.kills_it: One explosive — BUF has allowed 9 passes of 20+ on 83 attempts — or a no-blitz script where his 5.5 targets per game finally connect and clear 36.5.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so step 8 cannot size a rung and any implied 70%+ read is suspect on two-game samples. Cook's own pace (96 rush yards/game, 192 on 34 carries) disagrees with under 80.5; that is a flag, not a cut, because the read is the 5.65 vs 3.14 YPC mismatch. Full regression is about 17 carries times 3.14 = 53; the under only needs him under 80.5, but the box score does not agree. Johnston's 24 yards on 11 targets agrees with under 36.5; no sim contradicts the lean. Kincaid 225 and Coleman 64 were not used to pick overs.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Cook: weeks 1-2 made LAC's 3.14 YPC look stouter than it is, BUF was ahead early, and Cook ran 22 times for 90-plus with a 25-yarder — the 5.65 YPC traveled and flip 1 showed up, which the missing spread could not warn on. Allen did not vulture; he added carries beside Cook. Johnston: the blitz didn't finish or Herbert beat it, and one of those 103 air yards became a 40-plus catch against a BUF secondary that had already allowed 9 passes of 20+ on 83 attempts. A yards under on a deep threat with no posted price is a one-play leg; that counter is why Johnston is a lean, not a strong, and why he is the first cut if the blitz rate comes in well under 33%.
slip_story: One physical, blitz-and-stuffed-run script, not a shootout stack. Cook rush under and Johnston recyds under win together if LAC holds the run near 3.14 YPC and BUF's 33% blitz keeps Herbert off deep shots. Do not add Kincaid, Moore, McConkey, or Harris overs — those need chunk plays and the opposite environment — and do not add a total, which is not in the pack. No TDs. Provisional until inactives, which are not in the pack.
